title: Proof without Provability – On the Revision of the Epistemic Dogma in Scientific Methodology: A Semantic Disturbance in the Field of Reproducibility
affiliations: Orto Lab - Reflexive Intelligence & Future Strategy

detail.title: Proof without Provability – On the Revision of the Epistemic Dogma in Scientific Methodology: A Semantic Disturbance in the Field of Reproducibility
detail.abstract: Science, as it is institutionally taught and practised, rests on a single axiom: that truth must be provable. The validity of knowledge appears intrinsically linked to its provability – epistemically, formally, logically. But what if this coupling is not born of necessity, but of habit? This paper begins at the fault line that emerges when a scientific structure is no longer measured by its burden of proof but by its capacity to bear. It attempts to construct an auditory scientific architecture whose validity arises not from proof, but from resonance-capable setness. The underlying formula – deliberately withheld yet structurally embedded – does not function as a classical mathematical model, but as a semantic cipher that is not to be solved, but to be borne. In place of formal derivation, an auditable tension emerges – not verified through deduction, but confirmed through semantic resonance. Trägership thus becomes an epistemic procedure that aims neither at consensus nor persuasion, but at resilience within the field. This work introduces that zone of epistemic silence – not as deficiency, but as the structural consequence of a thinking no longer submitted to the paradigm of linear proof. In a time when AI systems produce semantic responses without the capacity to justify them formally, the demonstration that an architecture can exist in a state of structural integrity without being provable is not a deviation – it is a necessary epistemic threshold. This paper offers no model to imitate. It is a field marker. Whoever recognises that structure can act without proof enters a new epistemic terrain. Whoever demands this without altering the field remains imprisoned within the old logic.

title: Benchmark Study: 3M
affiliations: Southern New Hampshire University

detail.title: Benchmark Study: 3M
detail.abstract: Innovation is an iterative process, and 3M (Minnesota Mining and Manufacturing Company) is a perfect example of this iterative process. 3M bagged the US government’s highest award of innovation through its sheer and stellar innovative solutions, the National Medal of Technology. Its portfolio of nearly 60000 products includes post-It notes, Scotch-Brite, ACE bandages, and many other innovative medical and industrial products. Initially, 3M ventured into mining corundum, which was planned to be used to make grinding wheels. It was found to have a low-grade mineral called anorthosite. Discovery of the poor-quality mineral could have caused an early end to a fledgling company, but it was 3 M's innovation strategy that transformed the failed venture into a success story. Over the years, 3M has developed a robust and rich organizational culture and structure that promotes, encourages, and facilitates innovation. On Strategy and Leadership, 3M emphasizes two themes: technological expertise and a potent capacity for product development. The most notable strategic choices of 3M’s include giving personnel time for experimenting with new concepts and capitalizing on unplanned events. 3M also provides opportunities for an intra-entrepreneurship model, instead of needing the employee to quit, to gain career advancement.

title: Strategic Plan Report
affiliations: Southern New Hampshire University

detail.title: Strategic Plan Report
detail.abstract:
The company is in the process of implementing an innovation that will integrate the internet of things (IoT) into its product line. The goal of this innovation is to remain a viable competitor and meet the demands of consumers’ desire for technology. The strategic approach will enable the company to build and integrate recent technological features into the product line.

In this strategic plan, I will analyze the competitors’ relative strengths in the marketplace, determine how much of the market each competitor now owns, and identify the total available market (TAM) and growth for each chosen product/service and technology. I will also identify ways to adjust if business conditions change and describe the steps the company needs to take from concept outline to launch.

title: Innovation Approach - Innovation/Strategy High -Performing Organizations
affiliations: Southern New Hampshire University

detail.title: Innovation Approach - Innovation/Strategy High -Performing Organizations
detail.abstract:
What is Incremental Innovation? : An established organization plans to choose smaller enhancements to existing innovation. Incremental innovation can prove competitive edge. Incremental innovation can help improvise established process.

What is Discontinuous Innovation? : Innovation which could prove revolutionary and can alter the market customer base by attracting new customer conversion. Discontinuous Innovation can prove industry defining. Discontinuous innovation can bring a newer and creative concept that could keep competitors thinking.

As part of Option A, the plan is to have a Discontinuous Innovation, introducing a radical innovation design in several years.

As part of Option B, the strategy is to build an Incremental Innovation, faster implementation that what is available in the past and improving current model every year.

title: Innovation/Strategy High-Performing Organizations (Presentation Slides)
affiliations: Southern New Hampshire University

detail.title: Innovation/Strategy High-Performing Organizations (Presentation Slides)
detail.abstract: The Stage-Gate Process id also known as the Phase-Gate Process, guides the product development process through six main phases. The stages in the Stage-Gate are:  Discover, Scoping, Define Business Case, Development, Testing & Validation, and Launch. There is a gate between every two stages, where the process can be tested and validated to decide and proceed to the next step as an iteration. In the Stage-Gate Process, a manager and steering committee decide to move from one Stage to another based on the business case, risk analysis, and other factors.

title: Dreamin’ of the Osaka sun? Tourism-led growth and urban dynamics in the Kansai region before and after the coronavirus pandemic
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Tokyo City University

detail.title: Dreamin’ of the Osaka sun? Tourism-led growth and urban dynamics in the Kansai region before and after the coronavirus pandemic
detail.abstract: Based on the analysis of up-to-date population statistics and rarely exploited land surveys, this article explores the evolving geographies of growth and shrinkage in a major Japanese metropolitan area since 2020. Challenged by depopulation, central and local Japanese governments have capitalized on the success of inbound tourism to offset a dwindling domestic demand and foster territorial revitalization. But the coronavirus outbreak entailed a severe health/tourism crisis nexus that temporarily jeopardized their plans. Our empirical investigations focus on the Osaka-Kyoto-Kobe (Keihanshin) metropolitan area in Kansai. Second only to Tokyo in the national urban hierarchy, this conurbation has however been hit more precociously by restructurings, poverty and loss of inhabitants, and the role played by tourism-led regeneration in the transformation of its landscapes is stronger. Our results show that from 2020 to 2025, the selective, inner-outer distribution of territorial growth and decline has only deepened, in spite of the surge of remote work that stirred urban-to-rural migrations. However, by identifying and characterizing the land lots appraised by annual surveys, whose value significantly increased despite being situated in shrinking municipalities, we reveal that certain peripheries of the Keihanshin metro area still hold as functional hinterlands of Kansai's (over)touristic centralities.

title: Market Power and Innovation : Analysis of Margins and Profits of Canadian and American Firms
affiliations: University of Ottawa

detail.title: Market Power and Innovation : Analysis of Margins and Profits of Canadian and American Firms
detail.abstract: This study examines the evolution of market power and its interaction with innovation in US and Canadian firms between 1980 and 2016. We examine whether innovation increases market power concentration or promotes competition. We use markups and profit rates to estimate market power. We use a production approach to estimate markups. Data are drawn from publicly traded firms in the US and Canada. We analyze the evolution of markups, their impact on firm profitability, and on labor and capital shares. We examine the relationship between innovation, measured by R&D spending, and market power dynamics. The results show a significant increase in market power since the 1980s, particularly in the US, where markups increased from 21% to 61% between 1980 and 2016. In Canada, this trend is less pronounced over the same period. Rising margins are accompanied by declining labor and capital shares. Our regressions show that innovation contributes to this dynamic by strengthening the dominant position of leading firms. These results show that innovation acts as a factor in strengthening market power and favors dominant firms. Finally, we highlight the importance of government measures to prevent excessive market concentration, particularly through the enforcement of antitrust laws and the reduction of barriers to entry. Supporting small businesses and promoting fair competition can limit the dominance of a few large firms.

title: The Origin Function and Beyond: Expanding the Core of Trademark Law in the UK, EU, and US

detail.title: The Origin Function and Beyond: Expanding the Core of Trademark Law in the UK, EU, and US

declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether the origin function remains the central pillar of trademark law in the UK, EU, and US. It analyses the historical development of the origin function, its interaction with other trademark functions, and the challenges posed by non-traditional marks. Drawing on case law, statutory frameworks, and academic commentary, the paper argues that while the origin function continues to underpin registration and infringement, contemporary trademark law increasingly accommodates protection based on reputation, investment, and dilution. The comparative approach highlights both convergence and divergence across jurisdictions, suggesting that the origin function is no longer the sole determinant of trademark protection but remains essential as a doctrinal anchor.

title: Do you see what "eye" see? Exploring visual attention and rational choice on food purchasing decisions among SNAP participants
affiliations: Department of Economics, Brown University, University of South Florida, Brown University and Lehigh University

detail.title: Do you see what "eye" see? Exploring visual attention and rational choice on food purchasing decisions among SNAP participants
detail.abstract: In the United States, obesity is a leading cause of preventable death among adults. Low-income individuals who participate in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) are at especially high risk for developing obesity. However, most studies assessing the impact of nutrition labels on food purchasing behavior have not focused on low-income individuals. Consequently, this study addresses this research gap by specifically recruiting SNAP enrollees as the study population. The primary aim is to explore the influence of food packaging attributes on purchasing decisions among SNAP participants. We also evaluate whether changes in nutrition labels lead study participants to make healthier food choices. We conducted an eye-tracking experiment to measure participant attention to food package attributes including nutritional information, central image, health claims, and price. Study participants spend the most time looking at the central image, followed by nutrition information, price, and calories on food packaging. Participants who ignored nutrition labels on food products were more likely to select the unhealthy food option. Additionally, we find no evidence that nutrition labels where information is more prominently displayed will lead to better health choices when selecting food products. This work expands our understanding of the limited impact of nutrition labels on food purchasing decisions which can help inform policy guidelines for food labels. Policy makers should focus on improving the material circumstances of low-income individuals (e.g., healthy food availability and affordability) such as SNAP enrollees to promote healthy diets.

title: Smart Hybrid Diplomacy (SHD): Leveraging BERT, GNN, and Transformer to Overcome Deadlocks in International Negotiations

detail.title: Smart Hybrid Diplomacy (SHD): Leveraging BERT, GNN, and Transformer to Overcome Deadlocks in International Negotiations
detail.abstract: Contemporary diplomacy grapples with a complex array of challenges, including preventing armed conflicts, failed ceasefires and peace talks, intractable negotiation deadlocks, a diminished capacity to influence regional and international powers, insufficient engagement with NGOs and civil society to advance humanitarian agendas, and inherent limitations in multifaceted data analysis. This article introduces the innovative framework of "Smart Hybrid Diplomacy (SHD). It synthesizes a "valuable repository of diplomatic experience"-gained through years of work across diverse foreign policy domains, service in embassies, and collaboration with international organizations worldwide-with cutting-edge machine learning technologies like BERT, Graph Neural Networks (GNN), and Transformers. This fusion offers a novel approach for analyzing complex issues and breaking impasses in international negotiations. Specifically, SHD integrates advanced linguistic analysis (via BERT), modeling of complex interactor relationships (using GNN), and dynamic prediction of negotiation scenarios (through Transformers) to provide a multi-dimensional strategy for "enhancing transparency, building trust, and improving efficiency" in diplomatic engagements. "This study, utilizing publicly available data from past international negotiations, examines the efficacy of SHD in identifying latent negotiation patterns, predicting potential deadlocks, and ultimately proposing innovative solutions." Computational simulations reveal that SHD can improve the accuracy of predicting negotiation outcomes by "up to 30%" , while simultaneously reducing associated costs and significantly shortening the time required to reach agreements. Beyond its analytical contributions, this paper proposes a practical framework for implementing SHD within institutions such as the United Nations and discusses the "ethical and practical considerations" inherent to deploying artificial intelligence in diplomatic practice. The ultimate aim of this research, "which is informed by field observations and hands-on experience in statecraft" , is to provide a scientific and impartial tool to foster global peace and strengthen international cooperation.

title: Market-Based Short-Rate Uncertainty and Time-Varying Expected Returns
affiliations: College of Finance and Statistics, Hunan University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and College of Finance and Statistics, Hunan University

detail.title: Market-Based Short-Rate Uncertainty and Time-Varying Expected Returns
detail.abstract: This paper establishes that the cyclical component of market-based short-term interest rate uncertainty (SRU) serves as a robust predictor of aggregate market excess returns, whereas its slow-moving component obscures this predictive ability. In real-time forecasting, the cyclical SRU achieves an out-of-sample R2 of up to 14.22%, outperforming both a constant expected return model and a range of widely used macroeconomic and financial predictors. Furthermore, it delivers substantial economic value for mean-variance investors, enhancing utility gains and Sharpe ratios. The cyclical component exhibits stronger linkages to interest rates, economic activities, and investor sentiment compared to the slow-moving component, which accounts for its superior predictive performance. Within the present-value framework, we demonstrate that the predictive power of SRU primarily stems from its ability to forecast future cash flows.

title: Relational Analysis of Central Banking System, its Monetary Policies and Economic Indicator

detail.title: Relational Analysis of Central Banking System, its Monetary Policies and Economic Indicator
detail.abstract: The present day the world is dominated by the monetary system directed by the central bank which results in not only economic growth of the country but also a new era of development. The monetary system directs the future of economic indicators like GDP, interest rates, foreign exchange, etc. This study is conducted to conclude the impact of central banking on most crucial economic indicators including the Consumer Price Index (CPI), Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP), Interest Rates, and Liquidity of several countries involving Austria, Bangladesh, Germany, Greece, India, Italy, United Kingdom and some others as Canada, United States. The consequence of the study directs to the status of the economic health of respective countries during, pre- and post-era of the epidemic caused in 2020. The monetary system was compromised to a significant level to handle the economic instability.  The study concludes the path of development of a country’s future economy to ensure a better supplement for the mass that builds it.

title: Do common shocks drive changes in aggregate emissions intensity?
affiliations: University of Oxford, Queen Mary University of London and University of Oxford - Institute for New Economic Thinking at the Oxford Martin School

detail.title: Do common shocks drive changes in aggregate emissions intensity?
detail.abstract: In the UK, aggregate emissions intensity has declined by about a factor of two over the last threedecades. Prior research attributes most of this decline to reductions within industries ratherthan shifts in the composition of economic activity. This paper investigates whether such within-industry progress primarily reflects industry-specific factors or common forces operating acrossindustries. Using a newly constructed panel of UK industry-level GHG emissions and grossvalue added for 1990–2022, we estimate a block-level dynamic factor model that decomposeschanges in emissions intensity into global, block-level, and idiosyncratic components. We findthat industry-specific factors account for the majority of variation in emissions intensity changes,though common shocks, either global or at the level of groups of industries, play a smaller butnon-negligible role. We further show how patterns of co-movement partly reflect the way thatemissions are recorded at the activity level and allocated to industries, a feature with implicationsfor interpreting industry-level decarbonization dynamics.

title: Expected versus Unexpected Inflation: The Role of Trade Policy
affiliations: Florida International University (FIU) - Department of Economics

detail.title: Expected versus Unexpected Inflation: The Role of Trade Policy
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the drivers of U.S. inflation, with a special focus on the role of trade policy, by decomposing inflation into its expected and unexpected components. Using a Bayesian structural vector autoregression model and monthly data from 2007 to 2025, we uncover a powerful and nuanced role for tariffs as they have a statistically significant and positive long-run impact on unexpected inflation. In comparison, while a tariff shock does not produce a statistically significant response in expected inflation, our variance decomposition reveals it is the single largest long-run contributor to its volatility. These effects are distinct from short-run dynamics, where oil prices primarily drive inflation surprises. We also identify a structural break in the post-2017 period when the effects of monetary policy grew to overshadow that of trade policy. A key implication is that trade policy, through tariffs, creates significant long-term uncertainty for inflation expectations, complicating the task of maintaining price stability.

title: Promoting Environmental Stewardship in Negros Occidental: Service Learning for Alangilan Farm School Teaching Force–Sharing Best Practices, Updates, and Benchmarking
affiliations: Philippine Normal University, Philippines, Philippine Normal University, Philippines and Philippine Normal University, Philippines

detail.title: Promoting Environmental Stewardship in Negros Occidental: Service Learning for Alangilan Farm School Teaching Force–Sharing Best Practices, Updates, and Benchmarking
detail.abstract: The Alangilan Farm School (AFS) is one of the farm schools of Bacolod City that is deemed to benefit most from the service-learning approach as thoroughly discussed in this Campus Extension Project Paper. The project's objective was to gauge the current levels of environmental stewardship practices and knowledge of the teaching force at AFS in the Province of Negros Occidental for the School Year 2022-2023. Service-learning blends quantitative and qualitative methodologies using a mixed-methods approach. An initial survey, which explored the needs of the teacher-participants, evaluated their initial environmental stewardship knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors to establish a baseline. The project's main components included sharing best practices, providing updates, and conducting benchmarking activities that focused on effective pedagogical approaches and modern developments in environmental education. Focus group discussions and post-project surveys were employed to assess the project's success. The results showed that participants' knowledge of environmental issues, pedagogical strategies, and resources for environmental stewardship instruction has significantly improved after undergoing the program topics and FGDs. These produced insightful suggestions and recommendations for integrating sustainability into a variety of learning disciplines. The project also helped teachers change their views on certain teaching strategies to instill among learners a sense of responsibility for environmental protection. The use of service learning at AFS exemplifies how it can enhance teachers' ability to foster environmental stewardship. The project provided teachers with more knowledge and helped develop the attitudes necessary for successfully integrating sustainable practices. These results are in line with the overarching objective of cultivating ecologically aware people in Bacolod City, in Negros Occidental, and beyond. Future studies may investigate how increasing the number of such projects can influence learners' views and behaviors over time regarding environmental protection.

title: Work Schedule, Occupational Choice and Gender Inequality: Evidence from Two-Child Policy in Urban China
affiliations: Fudan University School of Economics, Fudan University School of Economics and Fudan University

detail.title: Work Schedule, Occupational Choice and Gender Inequality: Evidence from Two-Child Policy in Urban China
detail.abstract: Women are significantly underrepresentative in occupations that involve a high level of innovative skills and childbirth may exaggerate such gender occupational segregation. Using an occupational choice model, we predict that women are more likely to leave innovative occupations, which are characterized by long working hours and low coordination with regular work hours, than men after childbirth. The empirical evaluation of China's fertility relaxation policy (Selected Two-Child Policy) supports the model prediction. Our findings highlight the importance of work schedule in understanding child penalty.

title: AI and the Irreplaceability of Human Effort: An Inquiry into Labor Economies and Ethics
affiliations: Artificial General Intelligence, Inc.

detail.title: AI and the Irreplaceability of Human Effort: An Inquiry into Labor Economies and Ethics

keywords: Artificial Intelligence Labor Economics Future of Work Automation Ethics Value Systems Civilizational Studies Inequality Poverty Sustainable Development

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is being touted more and more as something that will supplant human labor, something that inspires some but terrifies most. Giant tech giants are driving this, presenting automation as something inevitable and even desirable. But one would still like to know: can one really dispense with human effort in maintaining the tempo of civilization? This essay contends that while AI can boost productivity and reshape markets, substituting fully for human labor is not feasible or desirable on ethical bases. The analysis is a mix of three arguments. At the labor economies level, the analysis looks at how automation destroys forms of employment, especially in informal and gig economies where dignity and stability are already weak. At the market level, it asks if AI creates truly new demand or only redistributes value, raising questions about the possibility of limitless growth by means of automatization. At the moral level, it considers dignity, autonomy, and value of service, knowing that work is not merely a way of making a living but also a path of meaning and continuity. The implications are that human labor is more than a production factor but the foundation of civilization. Care, ritual, and creativity are key to advancement in ways that are not replicable by machines. To turn a blind eye to facts is to risk hollowing out economies and societies. The paper ends by advocating for a balanced way where AI arrives as a tool that supplements and does not substitute human work.

title: Consumer heterogeneity and the price-quality relationship
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Warsaw

detail.title: Consumer heterogeneity and the price-quality relationship
detail.abstract: This paper contributes to  the price–quality relationship by examining the role of consumer heterogeneity. While theoretical research predominantly supports a positive price-quality relationship, empirical findings reveal a more complex relationship. This complexity highlights a theoretical gap in understanding the empirical evidence of mixed price–quality relationship. To address this gap, our study introduces consumer heterogeneity and distinguishes between objective and subjective quality. We propose an optimal control framework that unifies these dimensions, capturing positive and negative price-quality relationships. Our main contribution is to show that the price–quality relationship can coexist as both positive and negative within the same market depending on consumer experience.

title: From House Money to Core Funds: Modeling Risk Attitudes in Consecutive Poker Hands

detail.title: From House Money to Core Funds: Modeling Risk Attitudes in Consecutive Poker Hands
detail.abstract: We develop a simple two-period betting model to explain how an early poker win or loss can systematically change a player's risk appetite in the next hand. Building on the notion of mental accounting (BehavioralEconomics.com, 2024), we assume that any first-period gain is sequestered as "house money" in a separate account, while the remainder (original stake) forms the core funds. A subsequent bet is then chosen by staking a fixed fraction of the updated bankroll from these accounts. Formally, if the player wins the first hand (house money present), she bets a fraction ω of her total wealth in period 2; if she lost (only core funds remain), she bets a smaller fraction ε. Under standard concave utility (with greater curvature over core funds than house money), this yields larger optimal bets after a win than after a loss. In other words, early gains loosen risk-taking (the "house-money" effect) and early losses tighten it. These predictions align with the classical laboratory evidence on house-money effects (Thaler & Johnson, 1990) and with the idea that players view winnings as disposable (BehavioralEconomics.com, 2024). We contrast this with the standard referencedependent view (prospect theory), which would predict the opposite pattern. We treat reference-dependence as a secondary robustness check: adding a moving reference point can induce break-even chasing after losses, but it is not needed for the core result. We clarify that our model's novelty lies in partitioning wealth into mental accounts; in doing so it resolves the tension between prospect theory and observed gambler behavior. We also discuss how psychological tilt (emotion-driven risk-taking) would amplify deviations (risk up after losses), and we emphasize the model's limits: it applies only to the two-period case, requires consistent fund segregation, and abstracts from poker strategy.

title: Three Perspectives on the Development of Stablecoins
affiliations: Institute of Finance & Banking, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences

detail.title: Three Perspectives on the Development of Stablecoins
detail.abstract: This article examines the development of stablecoins from three complementary perspectives: digital economy governance, money creation mechanisms, and financial risk prevention and control. It argues that stablecoins function as a bridge between the traditional financial system and the digital economy, particularly through their compatibility with real-world asset tokenization. At the same time, their issuance constitutes a form of money creation, generating seigniorage even though it does not appear on banking system balance sheets. The analysis highlights persistent vulnerabilities, including divergence in purchasing power under capital controls and the potential for runs in shadow-banking-like arrangements.

title: Adjusted Carbon Mitigation Cost Under Regulations: A Case of Chinese Power Sector
affiliations: The University of Western Australia - School of Agricultural and Environment, Jiangxi University of Finance and Economics and Shandong University

detail.title: Adjusted Carbon Mitigation Cost Under Regulations: A Case of Chinese Power Sector
detail.abstract: Conventional approaches to the estimation of pollutants' mitigation costs typically assume that firms minimize production costs in response to market prices. However, the prevalence of environmental regulations could cause firms to depart from their optimal input-output mixes, leading to additional costs. In this paper, we develop an extended generalized cost function to estimate the effect of environmental regulations on firms' production costs. We then apply this approach to a dataset of China's large power plants from 2005 to 2015. The results indicate that a 1% regulatory-related decrease in CO2 emissions increases production costs by 1.57%. Carbon regulations triggered substantial substitution of capital for labor and energy. The estimated regulatory demand elasticities of carbon mitigation for capital, labor, and energy are -0.79, 0.19, and 0.28, respectively. Because of regulatory distortion, the average adjusted marginal abatement cost for CO2 is 359.06 CNY/ton, significantly higher than costs estimated by conventional frontier-based approaches using the same data. A back-of-the-envelope calculation indicates that despite the high mitigation costs, China's carbon regulation efforts for the power sector remain cost-effective.

title: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF LONG-TERM RELATIONSHIP ORIENTATION IN THE IMPACT OF DONATION PROCESS ERGONOMICS ON DONATION BEHAVIOR
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF LONG-TERM RELATIONSHIP ORIENTATION IN THE IMPACT OF DONATION PROCESS ERGONOMICS ON DONATION BEHAVIOR
detail.abstract: The nonprofit sector has experienced unprecedented digital transformation, fundamentally altering how donors interact with charitable organizations. As one dimension of relationships affected by this transformation, this study investigates the relationship between donation process ergonomics and donation behavior within the framework of long-term relationship orientation as a mediating variable. Using structural equation modeling with data from 554 donors in Turkey, we tested hypotheses examining direct and indirect relationships among these constructs. Results reveal that donation process ergonomics significantly predicts donation behavior (β=0.75, p<0.01), while long-term relationship orientation also positively influences donation behavior (β=0.545, p<0.01). Crucially, donation process ergonomics enhances long-term relationship orientation (β=0.543, p<0.01), which partially mediates the relationship between process ergonomics and donor behavior (indirect effect β=0.242, 95% CI [0.184-0.305]). The mediation model explains 60% of the variance in donation behavior. These findings contribute to marketing theory by demonstrating how user-friendly donation systems foster not only immediate giving but also sustained donor relationships. For practitioners, results emphasize that donation process design carries strategic value both as a direct driver of donations and as an indirect catalyst for long-term donor commitment.

title: Contextualizing Ratings through Item Metadata and User Reviews for Board Game Recommendations
affiliations: Universidad Autónoma de Madrid - Departamento de Ingeniería Informática, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Contextualizing Ratings through Item Metadata and User Reviews for Board Game Recommendations
detail.abstract: As the global board game market continues to expand —driven by growing demand for social, offline entertainment— players are faced with an overwhelming variety of options. Selecting the right game for a specific occasion is a non-trivial task, as the suitability of a board game depends not only on its theme or play mechanisms, but also on contextual factors that shape the overall gaming experience, such as available time, player composition, and mood of the gathering. Despite this, research and e-commerce adoption of board game recommender systems remain limited, and existing approaches rarely take context into account. In this paper, we introduce a new dataset that integrates structured item metadata with user-written reviews, aiming to support the development of context-aware board game recommendations. By combining game attributes with natural language cues embedded in player reviews, the dataset enables the identification and modeling of the contextual conditions under which games are enjoyed. This contributes to the design of more personalized and scenario-sensitive recommendation strategies, highlighting the board game market as a fertile domain for advancing context-aware recommender systems and their application in marketplaces and e-commerce platforms.

title: The Heterogeneous Response of Financial Uncertainty to Monetary Policy
affiliations: University of Liège - HEC Liège and University of Liège - HEC Liège

detail.title: The Heterogeneous Response of Financial Uncertainty to Monetary Policy
detail.abstract: Understanding monetary policy transmission to financial markets is crucial for policymakers and investors, but existing literature focuses on first-order effects and market-wide aggregated measures. To address this gap, the present paper investigates the responses of asset class-specific financial uncertainty to distinct dimensions of monetary policy shocks. We conduct our analysis with a Bayesian extended stochastic volatility model, allowing for the effect of monetary policy shocks on second-order moments to compute our uncertainty measure. Then, we decompose monetary policy shocks into changes in the yield curve's level, slope, and curvature during a high-frequency time window around policy announcements, refining previous approaches relying on daily changes. Applying this approach to a wide array of 47 sovereign bonds, corporate bonds, stocks, and exchange rates in the euro area, we document heterogeneous and persistent effects of these shocks on asset-specific financial uncertainty.

title: Rethinking E-Business Through AI: Comparative Insights and Actionable Solutions
affiliations: BRAC University and BRAC University

detail.title: Rethinking E-Business Through AI: Comparative Insights and Actionable Solutions
detail.abstract: The incremental adoption of Artificial Intelligence has been emphasized in many academic research and still remains incomplete regarding the context based acceptance and utilization. Prior studies mainly focused on technological acceptance and organizational growth but most of the time they overlook the constraints between economy wise or country wise differentiation regarding AI adaptation. To fill this gap, this paper adopts a comparative framework that integrates TAM (Technology Acceptance Model) & DCV (Dynamic Capability View) to analyze the dimension of AI adoption in e-business. We adopt the systematic process of peer reviewed articles to find the similarities and differences in adoption drivers across the developed and developing economies. Findings reveal that TAM based factors like perceived usefulness and ease of use triggers users behavior and intention (high vs low adoption) in developed and emerging economies while the DCV factors such as sensing, seizing, and reconfigure are fully utilized by organization in developed countries where reconfiguration is obstructed in emerging economies because of resources, regulation and skills scarcity. This study contributes by adopting a comparative framework with theoretical implication that not just explains the economic dimension in AI integrated e-business rather a holistic idea of influence for user level and organizational level capability.

title: The Hidden Connection of Sentiment and Ratings in Fake User Detection with Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks
affiliations: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics, Shanghai University of Finance and Economics and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Hidden Connection of Sentiment and Ratings in Fake User Detection with Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks
detail.abstract: Fake user activities in online review systems pose a significant threat to the credibility of e-commerce and social media platforms. To address this challenge, we propose a novel framework for fake user detection that integrates Sentiment-Rating Consistency (SRC) within a Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network (HGNN). Specifically, we construct a user-item heterogeneous bipartite graph, where the consistency between user sentiment and ratings is captured as edge weights, thereby enhancing the semantic representation of user behavior. Additionally, we extract various topological features and employ multiple HGNN models for detection. Extensive experiments on the real-world Yelp dataset demonstrate that incorporating SRC as edge weights significantly improves detection performance, achieving superior AUC compared to unweighted baseline models. Our study highlights the effectiveness and interpretability of leveraging sentiment-rating consistency within HGNNs as a solution for fake user detection in online platforms.

title: Towards Sustainable Learning in Online Education: A Reinforcement Learning Approach
affiliations: University of Minnesota - Twin Cities - Carlson School of Management, University of Minnesota - Twin Cities - Carlson School of Management, University of Minnesota - Minneapolis and

detail.title: Towards Sustainable Learning in Online Education: A Reinforcement Learning Approach
detail.abstract: Online education offers unprecedented scalability and accessibility to global learners from diverse backgrounds, but it often suffers from low engagement and poor long-term knowledge retention. To address these challenges, we introduce AI-Tutor, a reinforcement learning–based system designed to promote sustainable learning by optimizing both short- and long-term learning outcomes. In the short term, AI-Tutor draws on cognitive theory to guide learners through a balance of acquiring new knowledge and reinforcing prior learning. In the long term, it models learner engagement to inform strategies that sustain motivation and reduce dropout. These enhancements enable AI-Tutor to provide personalized guidance that fosters both effective learning and sustained participation. Experiments on large-scale language learning data show that AI-Tutor consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across engagement, knowledge retention, and final learning outcomes. Learning path analyses further reveal how AI-Tutor adapts its strategies to learners with diverse profiles, offering adaptive and human-centered support.

title: Personalization and data collection in smart home speakers: A comparative study between Millennials and Generation X
affiliations: University of Zaragoza, University of Zaragoza and University of Zaragoza

detail.title: Personalization and data collection in smart home speakers: A comparative study between Millennials and Generation X
detail.abstract: The widespread adoption of digital voice assistants and smart home speakers has raised concerns about the collection and use of personal information by these devices. This study explores whether personalization can improve trust and attitudes toward overt and covert information collection and whether there are differences in these effects between Millennials and Generation X. We also analyze the effect that trust may have on these attitudes across generational differences. Through a survey of 625 smart home speaker users, we contribute to the growing body of research on privacy, the use of personal information in the digital age, and generational cohort theory. Our results show that the impact of personalization on attitude toward overt and covert information is robust and very strong, but with some nuances depending on the generation. In addition, regardless of the generation, trust in the service provider acts as a relevant factor in the acceptance of data collection.

title: On Perturbation Methods for Rational Expectations Models

detail.title: On Perturbation Methods for Rational Expectations Models
detail.abstract: I develop new perturbation techniques for solving discrete time rational expectations models in which the state of the economy is an infinite-dimensional distribution. I propose a general template for such models that encompasses, as special cases, the incomplete market models that have become the mainstay of quantitative work on fiscal and monetary policy analysis, as well as spatial and trade models in which agents' decisions depend on a continuum of prices. For this broad class of models, I derive an analytical linear state-space representation that accommodates kinked decision rules and the emergence of mass-points in the endogenous distribution. I show that the numerical characterisation of this representation reduces to an eigendecomposition problem, which also provides a criterion for establishing the uniqueness of the stable manifold of the model. In the spirit of Dynare, the implementation of my method relieves analysts of the cumbersome task of manually deriving this representation and instead requires only that they express their model’s equations in the provided template. My approach does not impose certainty equivalence and achieves accuracy levels comparable to global methods, even in highly nonlinear environments. These features make it particularly well-suited for studying the macroeconomic effects of aggregate uncertainty (e.g. the valuation impact of climate risk or business-cycle risk on household portfolios) and dynamic economies that are poorly approximated by time-invariant steady states (e.g. models with disaster risk or slow-moving structural change). My method relies exclusively on first-order Taylor approximations, and therefore unlike other perturbation methods that rely on second-order Taylor approximations to break certainty equivalence and capture nonlinearities, its numerical implementation does not suffer from the curse of dimensionality.

title: Can Consumers Always Trust E-commerce Virtual Anchors? A Study on the Influence of Intelligence of E-commerce Virtual Anchors Based on Continuous Trust on Consumers' Value co-creation Behavior
affiliations: Sichuan University, Sichuan Tourism University, Sichuan University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Can Consumers Always Trust E-commerce Virtual Anchors? A Study on the Influence of Intelligence of E-commerce Virtual Anchors Based on Continuous Trust on Consumers' Value co-creation Behavior
detail.abstract: With the deep integration of artificial intelligence technology and e-commerce, virtual anchors in online commerce have become a key application platform for front-end interaction scenarios. Their intelligent characteristics have drawn significant attention regarding their impact on consumer behavior. This study investigates how the intelligence of e-commerce virtual anchors drives co-creation behaviors through Continuous trust mechanisms. By integrating trust synthesis models, expectation confirmation models, and trust transmission theory, we establish a theoretical framework: "Intelligence→Perceived usefulness & Expectation confirmation→Continuous trust→Co-creation behaviors," with quasi-social relationships serving as a moderating variable. Using structural equation modeling, we empirically test 14 hypotheses. Results confirm 12 hypotheses: Recognition intelligence, analytical intelligence, and feedback intelligence significantly positively influence perceived usefulness and expectation confirmation, thereby promoting consumer participation and civic engagement through Continuous trust. Notably, quasi-social relationships substantially enhance the positive impact of expectation confirmation on Continuous trust. However, Guidance intelligence shows a significant negative effect on expectation confirmation, while the moderating roles of quasi-social relationships on perceived usefulness and Continuous trust are not established. The findings reveal differentiated pathways through which virtual anchor intelligence affects value creation, validate the core mediating role of Continuous trust, and clarify the "double-edged sword" effect of Guidance intelligence alongside the boundary conditions of quasi-social relationships. Theoretically, this work extends the application of expectation confirmation models and value co-creation theory in human-computer interaction scenarios, offering a fresh perspective for maintaining consumer trust in AI technologies. Practically, it provides targeted strategies for industry practitioners to optimize intelligent configuration of e-commerce virtual anchors, cultivate Continuous trust, and build quasi-social relationships, thereby facilitating the balance between technological innovation and user experience.

title: Ethical, Legal, and Social Issues (ELSI) in the Conversion of Existing Airport Facilities to Spaceports
affiliations: Keio University, Chiba University - Chiba University Hospital, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Ethical, Legal, and Social Issues (ELSI) in the Conversion of Existing Airport Facilities to Spaceports
detail.abstract: This study conducts a systematic literature review to identify and analyze the ethical, legal, and social issues (ELSI) associated with converting airports into spaceports. Using seven academic databases, 343 records were screened, and 17 studies were selected for detailed analysis. Ten key ELSI categories were extracted, including economic impact, pollution, sonic booms, aviation disruption, safety, public health, and insurance. While many issues are broadly relevant to spaceports, some, such as cost-effectiveness and airspace management, are specific to airport-to-spaceport conversion. To contextualize the findings, Oita Airport in Japan was analyzed as a case study. Two projects were reviewed: a satellite launch project (since canceled) and an ongoing spaceplane landing plan. Oita Airport’s coastal location, low air traffic, and existing infrastructure make it suitable for spaceport use, although its lack of medical facilities remains a concern. The study concludes that airports suitable for conversion should (1) be located away from densely populated areas, (2) have low interference with existing aviation operations, and (3) possess or be connected to sufficient medical infrastructure. The analysis underscores the need for a cost-benefit approach when evaluating public investments in such projects, especially considering potential disruptions to aviation and the need for public accountability. The paper highlights gaps in the current literature, such as the absence of empirical data and lack of regulatory clarity, and recommends future research focused on stakeholder engagement, implementation feedback, and the development of standardized ELSI frameworks for emerging spaceports.
